title: Principal-surface contour biplots
text: principal surface (Hastie & Stuetzle, 1989) smooth curved two-dimensional manifold fitted data set, generalising first two principal components nonlinear structure. prinsurf fits surface displays biplot: samples plotted surface coordinates 𝛌i\boldsymbol\lambda_i, variable shown contour lines fitted coordinate function $\widehat{f\mkern-2mu}_j(\boldsymbol\lambda)$ plane. variable’s value sample read locating sample among contour lines, direct nonlinear generalisation reading straight biplot axis.

what: Fitting a surface and drawing the biplot
title: Principal-surface contour biplots
text: vars argument, plot() draws bare scatter sample coordinates:  Passing vars adds one panel per named variable, variable’s contour lines sample coordinates:  subset can requested:  panel titled variable’s name default. main replaces titles – one string every panel, one per panel order vars – outer_main puts single title figure whole:
code: library(prinsurf)  fit <- prinsurf(iris[, 1:4], scale = TRUE)   # standardise heterogeneous units fit #> Principal surface fit: 150 samples, 4 variables #>   loess span 0.60, converged in 10 iterations #>   variables: Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, Petal.Length, Petal.Width plot(fit, group = iris$Species) plot(fit, vars = colnames(iris)[1:4], group = iris$Species) plot(fit, vars = c("Petal.Length", "Petal.Width"), group = iris$Species) plot(fit, vars = c("Petal.Length", "Petal.Width"), group = iris$Species,      main = c("Petal length (cm)", "Petal width (cm)"),      outer_main = "Iris contour biplot")

what: Reading the variables: predict() and its error
title: Principal-surface contour biplots
text: predict() reads every variable’s value sample variable’s contour lines sample’s biplot position 𝛌i\boldsymbol\lambda_i, interpolation used draw contours returns n×pn \times p matrix variables’ original scales. Values come contour grid alone; sample whose position covered supported part grid contours read returned NA. Note predict() fitted() answer different questions. fitted() gives $\widehat{f\mkern-2mu}(\boldsymbol\lambda_i)$ exactly, centred/scaled units used fitting – surface’s reconstruction sample. predict() gives reader interpolating printed contour lines obtain, original measurement scales. contour_predictive_error() measures reading samples’ actual values, per variable, root-mean-square error working (centred/scaled) units:

title: Principal-surface contour biplots
text: Two diagnostics look surface fit different angles: contour_predictive_error() measures reading one variable time contours, sample predictivity asks well surface reconstructs whole sample, $\widehat{\boldsymbol x\mkern-3mu}_i = \widehat{f\mkern-2mu}(\boldsymbol\lambda_i)$, proportion sample’s squared length fit recovers, $1 - \lVert \boldsymbol x_i - \widehat{f\mkern-2mu}(\boldsymbol\lambda_i) \rVert^2 / \lVert \boldsymbol x_i \rVert^2$. read sample’s position surface principal-surface analogue biplot sample predictivity. curved surface reconstructs samples better flat PCA biplot, captures nonlinear structure plane .
code: pred <- predictivity(fit) summary(pred) #>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.  #>  0.5423  0.9193  0.9792  0.9377  0.9947  0.9998 attr(pred, "overall") #> [1] 0.9377464  ## PCA biplot (rank-2) sample predictivity on the same standardised data, for comparison Z   <- scale(as.matrix(iris[, 1:4])) V2  <- svd(Z)$v[, 1:2]; Zhat <- Z %*% V2 %*% t(V2) pca <- mean(1 - rowSums((Z - Zhat)^2) / rowSums(Z^2))  c(principal_surface = round(attr(pred, "overall"), 3), pca_biplot = round(pca, 3)) #> principal_surface        pca_biplot  #>             0.938             0.918

what: Contour biplot versus a PCA biplot
title: Principal-surface contour biplots
text: PCA biplot represents every variable single straight axis, can show structure linear two leading principal components. upper cap sphere makes contrast contour biplot concrete: height coordinate x interior maximum fitted surface (closed, concentric contours), y z vary monotonically.  x’s closed contours visible directly; y z show open, roughly parallel contours. PCA biplot data, drawn biplotEZ, shows flat, straight-axis representation structure:  samples form hollow ring: two leading principal components recover y z, x almost orthogonal plane collapses near-zero variation across . Every sample near middle height range sits close spot regardless actual x, straight axis x express interior maximum. contour biplot’s curved surface follows maximum instead flattening away. Sample predictivity makes point numerically, unlike near-planar iris data gap large:
code: ## upper cap of a sphere: x = height, y, z = horizontals n <- 200; u <- 2 * runif(n) - 1; th <- 2 * pi * runif(n) - pi S <- cbind(x = u, y = sin(th) * sqrt(1 - u^2), z = cos(th) * sqrt(1 - u^2)) S <- S[S[, "x"] > -0.4, ]                 # keep the cap S <- sweep(S, 2, colMeans(S))             # centre sph <- prinsurf(S, max.iter = 8) plot(sph, vars = colnames(S)) biplotEZ::biplot(data = S) |> biplotEZ::PCA() |> plot() ps  <- mean(predictivity(sph))  Zc  <- scale(S, scale = FALSE) V2  <- svd(Zc)$v[, 1:2]; Zhat <- Zc %*% V2 %*% t(V2) pca <- mean(1 - rowSums((Zc - Zhat)^2) / rowSums(Zc^2))  c(principal_surface = round(ps, 3), pca_biplot = round(pca, 3)) #> principal_surface        pca_biplot  #>             0.977             0.818

title: Plot a principal-surface biplot — plot.prinsurf
code: set.seed(1) s <- runif(120, -1, 1); t <- runif(120, -1, 1) X <- cbind(x = s, y = t, z = 0.7 * s + 0.9 * t^2) +      matrix(rnorm(360, 0, 0.03), 120, 3) fit <- prinsurf(X, max.iter = 6)  ## default: each panel is titled with its variable's name plot(fit, vars = c("x", "z"))   ## your own panel titles, and a title for the figure as a whole plot(fit, vars = c("x", "z"),      main = c("First coordinate", "Third coordinate"),      outer_main = "Principal-surface biplot")   ## a title on a single, contour-free panel plot(fit, main = "Sample coordinates")

title: prinsurf 2.0
text: Principal surface fits now displayed contour biplots. plot() draws variable contour lines fitted surface coordinate function f_j, variable’s value read contours sample’s position surface, place linear axes conventional biplot. plot() gains arguments tailoring display: vars select variables drawn, group colour samples factor, nlevels col_contour control contour axes, main / outer_main title individual panels overall figure. predictivity() reports sample predictivity — proportion sample’s squared length reconstructed fitted surface. per-sample values returned vector, mean samples "overall" attribute. contour_predictive_error() reports, variable, root-mean-square difference value read contour lines sample’s actual value. measures accurately variable can recovered reading contours; mean variables "overall" attribute. predict() returns values read contour axes sample’s position, back-transformed variables’ original scales. fitted() returns fitted surface coordinates f_j(lambda_i) every sample variable, working (centred / scaled) units. print() summarises fit: number samples variables, loess span, number iterations convergence, variable names.
